original_question: Let f : PN 99K PN be a dominant rational map defined over Fq . (a) PN (F̄q )f is Zariski dense in PN . (b) lim #PN (Fqk )f /#PN (Fqk ) = 1. k→∞.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 18.10 in Section 18 ("Dynamics over Finite Fields"); the draft is targeting this conjecture, not the paper's Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the exact finite-field conjecture in the paper: a dominant rational self-map f of projective space over F_q, together with the two claims that (a) the set P^N(Fbar_q)_f is Zariski dense in P^N and (b) the proportion #P^N(F_{q^k})_f / #P^N(F_{q^k}) tends to 1 as k -> infinity. Those are precisely the two parts of Conjecture 18.10.
missing_details: The notation P^N(K)_f is not defined. In the paper this means the set of points whose forward orbit under f is well-defined and avoids the indeterminacy locus of f; earlier the general notation is given as P^N_f = {P in P^N : f^n(P) notin I(f) for all n >= 0}, and with coordinates in K one writes P^N(K)_f.
The indeterminacy locus I(f) is not defined. For a rational map f=[f_0,...,f_N], it is the subset where all coordinate functions vanish simultaneously.
The draft should explicitly say that q is a prime power and that Fbar_q denotes an algebraic closure of F_q.
The ambient dimension N >= 1 is implicit but should be stated.
To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to say that f is a rational self-map of projective N-space over F_q, given by homogeneous coordinate functions of the same degree.
The limit in part (b) should be stated as k ranging over positive integers.
The phrase "Zariski dense" is used correctly, but in a stand-alone formulation it should be clear that the density is in the ambient projective space P^N with its Zariski topology.
The draft does not mention the nearby paper remark that part (b) implies part (a); this is not needed in the final question, but it is relevant context for how the paper organizes the conjecture.
refined_question: Let q be a prime power, let N >= 1, let Fbar_q be an algebraic closure of F_q, and let f=[f_0:...:f_N]: P^N dashrightarrow P^N be a dominant rational self-map defined over F_q, where the f_i are homogeneous polynomials of the same degree and I(f) = {f_0 = ... = f_N = 0} is the indeterminacy locus. For any extension field K/F_q, define P^N(K)_f to be the set of points P in P^N(K) whose forward orbit under f is well-defined, equivalently such that f^n(P) notin I(f) for every n >= 0. Is it true that: (a) P^N(Fbar_q)_f is Zariski dense in P^N; and (b) lim_{k->infty} #P^N(F_{q^k})_f / #P^N(F_{q^k}) = 1, where k runs over the positive integers?
justification: The draft matches Conjecture 18.10 almost verbatim in both parts, so the nearest official formulation is Conjecture 18.10 itself in Section 18. The only substantial omissions are the paper's standing notation for points with well-defined forward orbit, the role of the indeterminacy locus I(f), and the basic field data F_q and Fbar_q. The paragraph immediately before Conjecture 18.10 recalls that one must exclude points whose orbit lands in I(f), and Remark 18.11 immediately after the conjecture notes that part (b) implies part (a), but the paper does not state an equivalence, so there is no paper-explicit alternate equivalent formulation to give.
